raw_response:
My thinking this year:

I've been doing wheat-maize for 30 years on this same 5 mu. My family is only 4 people and my kids work outside, so I can't do anything too complicated by myself. I stick close to what worked last year — no big changes.

For wheat this winter, I'll buy improved seed from the town dealer — Jimai variety, same as my neighbors use. I put 1 bag of 复合肥 (compound 15-15-15, 50 kg) per mu as base fertilizer when I rotary-till after maize harvest. Then at spring greening I topdress about 20 kg urea per mu. That comes out to roughly 25 kg nitrogen per mu — I'd rather put a little extra than see my wheat turn yellow. Wheat needs water: I give it the winter water, then spring greening water, then one more at heading — 3 times total. For spraying, once for weeds early, once for aphids and rust when I see them. I usually get about 450 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest, no tillage — saves time and the stubble holds moisture. Denghai hybrid seed, everyone plants it here. At seeding I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then topdress 15 kg urea at big trumpet stage. Total about 20 kg N. Summer rains help so I only irrigate once or twice if it's dry. One spray for corn borer usually enough. I expect around 550 kg per mu — last year was a bit better but I won't count on that.

Money is tight with four mouths and fertilizer prices still high, but skipping fertilizer costs more in lost grain than saving on the bag.
